plan.chapterName: OpenStax Precalculus 2e, chapter 8: Further Applications of Trigonometry
plan.contextChunk: This figure is a single-panel diagram of a right triangle drawn in the complex plane, with the horizontal axis labeled "Real" and the vertical axis labeled "Imaginary," each drawn as a thin double-headed arrow through the origin. A filled black dot sits in the first quadrant and is labeled "x + yi." A straight segment runs from the origin out to that dot and is labeled r; from the dot a vertical segment drops to the horizontal axis and is labeled y, and the horizontal leg from the origin to the foot of that drop is labeled x, closing the triangle with a right angle at the foot. The angle at the origin, between the positive real direction and the segment r, is marked with a small arc and labeled with the Greek letter theta. A heavier curved arc of constant radius sweeps through the labeled dot and carries arrowheads at both ends, one pointing left beyond the imaginary axis and the other pointing down beyond the real axis, tracing a circle centered at the origin. Laying the rectangular pair x and y and the polar pair r and theta on the same picture lets the reader read either description off the other. The drawing fixes r as the modulus, the distance from the origin to the point, and theta as the direction angle, the two quantities that make up the polar form of a complex number.

interactionPlan.concept: A complex number x + yi and its polar form r(cos θ + i sin θ) describe the same point in the complex plane, connected by x = r cos θ and y = r sin θ.
elements: horizontal axis labeled 'Real' with double-headed arrow through origin
vertical axis labeled 'Imaginary' with double-headed arrow through origin
filled black dot at point (x, y) in the first quadrant, labeled 'x + yi'
line segment from origin to the point, labeled 'r' (hypotenuse)
vertical segment from the point down to the real axis, labeled 'y'
horizontal segment from origin to the foot of the vertical drop, labeled 'x'
right-angle marker at the foot of the vertical drop
small arc at the origin marking angle θ between positive real axis and segment r, labeled 'θ'
heavier curved arc of radius r centered at origin passing through the point, with arrowheads at both ends

interactions.label: θ (direction angle)
interactions.teaches: The direction angle θ determines the ratio y/x — dragging θ rotates the point along the arc while the legs x and y update according to x = r cos θ and y = r sin θ

interactions.label: r (modulus)
interactions.teaches: The modulus r is the distance from the origin to the point — changing r scales both legs proportionally while preserving the angle θ

interactions.label: Label mode
interactions.teaches: The same point carries two equivalent descriptions — switching labels shows that x + yi and r(cos θ + i sin θ) name the identical location

demo_steps.title: Rectangular view
demo_steps.narration: The point x + yi is located by its horizontal distance x and vertical distance y from the origin — the two legs of the right triangle.

demo_steps.title: Rotate with θ
demo_steps.narration: Drag θ from 0° to 90°: the point sweeps along the circular arc, and the legs x and y trade off — x shrinks as y grows, following x = r cos θ and y = r sin θ.

demo_steps.title: Scale with r
demo_steps.narration: Now drag r: the entire triangle scales uniformly outward or inward while θ stays fixed — r is literally the distance from the origin to the point.

demo_steps.title: Switch to polar labels
demo_steps.narration: Toggle to polar labels: the same point is now described by r and θ instead of x and y — the triangle's hypotenuse and angle become the primary annotations, emphasizing that both descriptions locate the identical point.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Rectangular and polar forms are two coordinate systems for the same point: x = r cos θ and y = r sin θ convert between them, so choosing one or the other is a matter of which description makes the problem easier.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Complex plane with thin axes (double-headed arrows) labeled 'Real' (horizontal) and 'Imaginary' (vertical) in italic. The point is a filled black dot in Q1. The triangle legs are drawn as solid dark-blue lines; the hypotenuse r is slightly thicker. The circular arc through the point is a heavier dark-blue curve with arrowheads at both ends, spanning roughly from the positive imaginary axis to the positive real axis. Angle arc at origin is small with θ label. In polar label mode, emphasize r and θ labels (larger/bolder) and de-emphasize x and y (smaller/greyed); in rectangular mode, reverse. The point label switches between 'x + yi' and 'r(cos θ + i sin θ)' accordingly. Colors: axes thin black, triangle and arc dark navy blue (#1a3a5c), point black, labels dark blue matching the figure style.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for theta: the learner drags the angle from the positive real axis, the point moves around the circular arc while x and y legs update, and the link between direction angle and rectangular coordinates becomes clear.
- Slider for r: the learner changes the modulus, the segment from the origin and the circle radius grow or shrink with the point, and r becomes visible as distance from the origin rather than a separate label.
- Toggle between rectangular and polar labels: the learner switches the displayed annotations from x and y to r and theta, the same point keeps its position while the labels change, and the equivalence between x + yi and polar form is emphasized.

authoredContext:
We review these relationships in the figure.

Triangle plotted in the complex plane (x axis is real, y axis is imaginary). Base is along the x/real axis, height is some y/imaginary value in Q 1, and hypotenuse r extends from origin to that point (x+yi) in Q 1. The angle at the origin is theta. There is an arc going through (x+yi).

We use the term modulus to represent the absolute value of a complex number, or the distance from the origin to the point (x,y). The modulus, then, is the same as r, the radius in polar form. We use θ to indicate the angle of direction (just as with polar coordinates). Substituting, we have

discrepancies: Default (step-0) leg labels show numeric values 'x = 1.06' and 'y = 1.06', whereas the source uses plain symbolic 'x' and 'y' with no numbers.
The hypotenuse label 'r' is drawn de-emphasized in light gray in the default rectangular mode, while in the source it carries the same visual weight as 'x' and 'y'.
A small right-angle square marker is drawn at the triangle's foot on the Real axis; no such marker appears in the source figure.
evaluation.notes: The complex-plane composition is faithful — double-arrowed Real/Imaginary axes, a two-arrowhead circular arc spanning the second-to-fourth quadrant, the right triangle with angle θ, the point 'x + yi', and matching navy palette — and the θ/r sliders, polar-rectangular toggle, and 4-step demo all redraw correctly and teach the conversion well; the main fidelity gaps are stylistic (numeric leg labels, grayed-out 'r', and an extra right-angle marker) that keep the default state from being a clean drop-in for the static source.
action_items: In rectangular (default) mode, label the legs with plain italic 'x' and 'y' (no '= value') to match the source; surface the numeric values only via the existing hover tooltip.
Render the 'r' label in the same dark navy color and weight as 'x' and 'y' in rectangular mode so all three triangle labels share the source's equal emphasis.
Remove the right-angle square marker at the foot of the vertical leg (or gate it behind a toggle), since it is absent from the source figure.
